resolved_findings.finding: The endpoint drift -theta/beta is asserted for a finite open chain without N>=2. The linked open-chain definition permits N=1, in which case there is no Gamma edge, a_{n_-}=0, and the drift is 0.

resolved_findings.finding: The quantitative infinite/open comparison omits the source hypothesis that K is an integer at least 1. The written inequalities permit T=K=0. At t=0 the right endpoint has a^I_{n_+}=0 but the infinite-chain a_{n_+} is an unbounded square-root Gamma variable. The claimed bound by 1 with probability at least 1-C exp(-c R^2), for arbitrarily large R, would then force a_{n_+}<=1 almost surely.

independent_checks.derivation: Open force is a_(i-1)^2-a_i^2 with missing edges zero. Periodic r'=p_(i+1)-p_i preserves sum r and has zero divergence. Energy bounds p and finite-time position/stretch increments. Fixed-stretch conditioning is not an independent product.
independent_checks.result: No finding. AGG-M01 and AGG-M02 resolved in the recorded revisions.

independent_checks.derivation: With B_(i,i+1)=-a_i/2, [B,L]_ii=a_(i-1)^2-a_i^2, [B,L]_(i,i+1)=a_i(b_i-b_(i+1))/2, and second bands cancel. U'=BU gives (U^T U)'=0 and (U^T L U)'=0. The diagonal of [B,L^m] is j_(i-1)-j_i.

The first component and recurrence determine a Jacobi eigenvector; zero endpoint forces the zero vector. Orthogonality and the (2N)^-1 threshold yield Hall's condition by a mass-counting contradiction; the two-case induction proves matching.

For Y=a^2, E Y^s=beta^-s Gamma(theta+s)/Gamma(theta). Thus E[-log Y]=log beta-psi(theta), Var(log Y)=psi'(theta), E Y=theta/beta. Trace L^2 gives second moment (1+2theta)/beta. L_beta has law beta^-1/2 L_1, so rho_beta(x)=sqrt(beta)rho_1(sqrt(beta)x).
independent_checks.result: No finding; changing beta is distinct from the fixed-beta small-theta regime.

independent_checks.derivation: Markov and the finite union retain N and zeta factors. Truncation residual has only endpoint contributions; expansion in an orthogonal eigenbasis yields distance to truncated spectrum <= residual norm/vector norm. Spectral leakage identity follows by interchanging finite sums.
independent_checks.result: No finding; stochastic localization itself remains cited.

independent_checks.derivation: The one-sided energy differs from (L^2)_ii by a_i^2-a_(i-1)^2. Arbitrary spatial-selected index sets can have many boundary components, so no unjustified two-endpoint telescoping is used.

For r=2 log[(2/Delta)cosh(Delta(t-t0)/2)], r''=2 exp(-r). The conserved eigenvalues are v+-Delta/2. Comparing fast-label asymptotes gives outgoing-minus-incoming shift -2 log Delta; the slow-label shift is +2 log Delta.

The first-row eigenvector equation gives (log w_j)'=b_left-lambda_j and normalization yields w_j(t) proportional to w_j(0)e^-lambda_j t. Jacobi determinant recurrence fixes product and logarithm signs. Subtracting the two assumed decay relations cancels the common left-end translation and adds at most 2E.
independent_checks.result: No finding; index-to-position reordering and uniform-time estimates remain additional cited inputs.

independent_checks.derivation: Compared fixed parameter dependence, both endpoint bulk conditions, threshold specialization, time range, initial-center buffer and simultaneous time/label event with S-v4. Overwhelming probability implies each fixed polynomial tail asymptotically.

Using A d0=1, A d1=x and rho=alpha*d0*h, eliminate the common theta^-1 term after multiplying the first equation by v=d1/d0. The result is x=v+(2/alpha) integral (v(x)-v(y))log|x-y|rho(y)dy. The reverse argument uses d0*v in H; reflection gives odd v.
independent_checks.result: No finding, conditional on explicitly cited operator inputs.

independent_checks.derivation: An even normalized mollifier gives chi(-x)=1-chi(x), so chi-H is odd and has zero integral. For x!=0, ell_d(x)-log|x|=0.5 log(1+d^2/x^2) lies between 0 and d^2/(2x^2). Deterministic-test fixed-time concentration is not promoted to one universal event over all times/tests.

The chain rule gives the stated S(x)x'=lambda identity. Choosing a maximal coordinate gives ||Sw||_infty>=delta||w||_infty. Given comparison and inverse/residual assumptions, integrate x'-v to obtain 2K sqrt(M)+K^2 T/sqrt(M); M=T gives the claimed order.
